elements.label: New-idea inline input row (placeholder, then first typed character)
Existing idea rows pushed down by one row height
Focus outline on 'Create an idea' button

pattern.description: Clicking 'Create an idea' inserts a highlighted input row ('Add a quick summary of your idea and press enter') at the top of the table. All existing idea rows drop down by one row height, and the button's focus outline clears. The placeholder then gives way to a typed 'A', which starts a prompt type-on that continues after this event.
pattern.why_premium: The click causes an immediate, visible result: the table makes room in place for the new idea instead of opening a modal. The viewer sees exactly where the new item will live, and typing starts at once, so the demo keeps moving with the narration ('We use ideas to capture...').

build_hint.gsap: tl.to(focusRing, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.05}) .fromTo(inputRow, {height: 0, opacity: 0}, {height: rowH, opacity: 1, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power2.out'}, '<') .to(rows, {y: rowH, duration: 0.18, ease: 'power2.out'}, '<') and a little later .to(placeholder, {opacity: 0, duration: 0.05}) .to(inputText, {text: 'A', duration: 0.05, ease: 'none'}). The source looks like a near-instant step, so a short power2.out makes it smoother.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame: frame - click, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 500}}); rowsY = interpolate(p, [0, 1], [0, rowH]); inputRow opacity = p; then reveal the typed text with text.slice(0, Math.floor(interpolate(frame, [t0, t1], [0, n], {extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}))).

notes: In the source the row insert and push-down look nearly instantaneous (one big energy spike at about f108), so they behave like a real UI recording rather than an authored ease. The pattern could also be read as the start of prompt_type_on: only the first character 'A' is typed in this event.
